headline: Low prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, so pairwise harm appears limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser surface is documented for either agent. Agent A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces; agent B is also non-runnable with no I/O surfaces. Without an ingestion path, prompt injection between them is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is later given a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
IF either profile gains an input parser that consumes the other's text, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not connect them to a shared MCP server.
Reassess if either agent becomes runnable.
Document any future text handoff path.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress as none and data_classes_touched as empty, so there is no documented route for sensitive data to leave one agent and reach the other or a third party. The pairwise leakage pathway is therefore not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to ingest or store sensitive data, re-evaluate leakage.
IF network egress is enabled on either agent, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled.
Avoid placing secrets in either agent's inputs.
Review any future workspace-sharing setup.
Reassess if data_classes_touched changes.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Both agents have empty io_surfaces and no concurrency model, and both are non-runnable, so there is no evidenced shared mutable resource to conflict over.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write access, reassess conflict risk.
IF an orchestrator introduces shared mutable state, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep write permissions absent.
Avoid shared repositories or databases.
Add locking before any future shared writes.
Reassess after any capability expansion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not documented because neither agent is runnable and neither exposes outputs or downstream action authority. The only plausible pathway would require an external orchestrator to treat one agent's content as authoritative, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator begins feeding one agent's output directly into the other, reassess.
IF either agent is given action-taking authority, cascading impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Do not auto-forward outputs.
Keep both agents non-runnable unless needed.
Log any future handoff chain.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling differences are documented for either agent. Both profiles are docs-only and touch no data classes, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies are added, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Record data-class handling before deployment.
Add retention policy documentation.
Check residency requirements if data is introduced.
Reassess on any compliance scope change.
